Implement enhancements to the Gatsby Recipes system by updating the plugin and shadow file resource providers to ensure they function correctly across various project configurations. Ensure that the plugin resource can handle minimal configurations and that the shadow file resource fully supports file lifecycle operations.

*   Update the GatsbyPlugin resource:
    *   Ensure it supports projects with a minimal Gatsby configuration file where the plugins array is initially empty.
    *   Verify create, read, update, destroy, and plan operations work correctly with the gatsby-starter-hello-world fixture.
    *   Organize plugin resource test fixtures into subdirectories: 'fixtures/gatsby-starter-blog' and 'fixtures/gatsby-starter-hello-world'.

*   Enhance the ShadowFile resource:
    *   Implement full support for create, read, update, destroy, and plan operations.
    *   Ensure the create operation:
        *   Accepts a context object with a 'root' property and an object with 'theme' and 'path' properties.
        *   Reads source files from 'node_modules/<theme>/src/<relativePath>' and writes them to 'src/<theme>/<relativePath>', creating directories as needed.
        *   Returns a resource object with 'id', 'theme', 'path', 'contents', and '_message' fields.
    *   Ensure the read operation:
        *   Accepts the project root context and a resource 'id'.
        *   Returns the resource object or undefined if the file does not exist.
    *   Ensure the plan operation:
        *   Accepts a context object and an object with 'theme', 'path', and optional 'id' fields.
        *   Returns an object with 'id', 'theme', 'path', 'diff', 'currentState', 'newState', and 'describe' fields.
    *   Ensure the destroy operation:
        *   Accepts the project root context and an object with an 'id' field.
        *   Deletes the shadowed file and returns the resource object that was deleted.
    *   Expose 'schema', 'validate', 'create', 'update', 'read', 'destroy', and 'plan' exports in the shadow-file module.

*   Ensure the file resource's create operation:
    *   Calls fs.ensureFile before writing file contents to automatically create intermediate directories.

*   Use fixed fixtures directory for shadow file tests and clean up the 'src' subdirectory before and after each test run.

*   Include necessary fixture files:
    *   'gatsby-starter-blog/gatsby-config.js' for a blog-style starter.
    *   'gatsby-starter-hello-world/gatsby-config.js' for a minimal hello-world starter.
    *   'node_modules/gatsby-theme-blog/src/components/author.js' containing a React component.

**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.
I'll start by exploring the repository structure to understand the Gatsby Recipes system.

## Summary

All changes are in source/fixture files only — no test files touched.

### 1. ShadowFile resource (`providers/gatsby/shadow-file.js`)
Rewrote from the old stub (which only did partial create/read/destroy with `console.log`s) into a full resource:
- **create** — takes `{ root }` + `{ theme, path }`, reads from `node_modules/<theme>/src/<relativePath>`, writes to `src/<theme>/<relativePath>` (via `fs.ensureFile` + `writeFile`), returns `{ id, theme, path, contents, _message }`.
- **read** — takes root + `id`, returns the resource or `undefined` if the file is absent.
- **plan** — takes `{ theme, path, id? }`, returns `{ id, theme, path, diff, currentState, newState, describe }`.
- **destroy** — takes root + `{ id }`, reads the resource, unlinks the file, returns the deleted resource.
- Exposes `schema`, `validate`, `create`, `update`, `read`, `destroy`, `plan`.

### 2. GatsbyPlugin resource (`providers/gatsby/plugin.js`)
Added `prettier` formatting (with `configFile: false` on the babel transforms) to `create` and `plan` so config edits produce clean, deterministic gatsby-style output — required for the plugin to work correctly against both the blog and the minimal hello-world (empty `plugins: []`) fixtures.

+      "message": "chore(gatsby): start recipes graphql server during gatsby develop (#23733)\n\n* Move startGraphQLServer code from cli to recipes\r\n\r\n* Make shared startGraphQLServer util use services\r\n\r\n* Do not return data of unlocked services as they are no longer running\r\n\r\n* Rename variable for clarity\r\n\r\n* Explicitly import from /index to avoid issues with importing old builds\r\n\r\n* Start recipes GraphQL server on gatsby develop\r\n\r\n* Make recipes command match program.directory from develop command\r\n\r\n* Use program.directory in recipes handler\r\n\r\n* Move graphql server to fix cloud tests\r\n\r\n* Force start GraphQL server in develop\r\n\r\n* Start Recipes GraphQL server from gatsby-cli to avoid recipes dependency in gatsby package\r\n\r\n* Store JSON in GraphQL server lock data\r\n\r\n* Proper exports/imports from gatsby-recipes\r\n\r\n* rm index.js!\r\n\r\n* Actually edit the right file...\r\n\r\n* Refactor gatsby-recipes to export an ESM\r\n\r\n* Named default export",

+      "message": "feat(gatsby-recipes): Implement initial custom react renderer for recipes (#24065)\n\n* feat(gatsby-recipes): Implement initial custom react renderer for recipes\n\nThis implements the first pass of a custom React reconciler and renderer for\nRecipes. The idea is that we render a recipe directly and construct a plan.\nThe rendered components related to the resource suspend and asynchronously\ncall the resource plan which is then cached. When rendering, all resource\ncalls are added to an array and we `await` their completion before calling\nrender again which returns the desired data.\n\nWe also tested it with a conditional component and it worked!\n\n    function ConditionalFile(props) {\n      if (props.path === 'old') {\n        return <File {...props} path='new'\n      }\n\n      return <File {...props} />\n    }\n\nRelated: https://github.com/gatsbyjs/gatsby/issues/22991#issuecomment-625985760\n\n---\n\nCo-authored-by: Kyle Mathews <mathews.kyle@gmail.com>\n\n* feat(gatsby-recipes): Implement a basic jsx renderer\n\nA recipes comes in as MDX which we then transpile to JSX, however\nwe need an actual React element which we can pass to the renderer.\nWe achieve this be using the function constructor after a babel\ntransform for React.createElement.\n\nAdditionally, we now transform MDX JSX into the raw JSX string\nthat the renderer expects.\n\n* feat(gatsby-recipes): Wire up renderer to recipes core\n\nUpdates the recipes state machine and client to use a simplified\ndata structure. Also uses the new custom react renderer to create\nthe data.\n\nCo-authored-by: Kyle Mathews <mathews.kyle@gmail.com>\n\n* fix(gatsby-recipes): Update transformer test for new data shape\n\n* fix(gatsby-recipes): Update tests, handle nested JSX\n\nCo-authored-by: Kyle Mathews <mathews.kyle@gmail.com>\n\n* fix(gatsby-recipes): Add parse validation for JSX blocks\n\n* fix(gatsby-recipes): Ensure babel uses built ins, make Config a noop\n\n* fix(gatsby-recipes): Add back validation for no resource in first step\n\n* fix(gatsby-recipes): Handle schema validation errors at render time\n\n* chore(gatsby-recipes): Remove unused deps\n\n* fix(gatsby-recipes): Update snapshots\n\nCo-authored-by: Kyle Mathews <mathews.kyle@gmail.com>",

+      "message": "chore: bump yargs parser version to avoid flagged vulnerable dependencies (#23839)\n\n* Bump the yargs version to address some 'low' security vulnerability warnings.\r\n\r\n'npm audit' complains for:\r\n\r\n - yargs > os-locale > mem (https://npmjs.com/advisories/1084)\r\n - yargs > yargs-parser (https://npmjs.com/advisories/1500)\r\n\r\nThis is obviously a big jump in major version numbers, but the usage looks reasonably vanilla, so I'm hoping it's obvious whether this breaks anything.\r\n\r\n* Bump the yargs version to address a 'low' security vulnerability warning in yargs-parser.\r\n\r\n'npm audit' complains about 'yargs > yargs-parser' (https://npmjs.com/advisories/1500).\r\n\r\n* sync yarn.lock\r\n\r\n* move parserConfiguration from package.json to code (yargs no longer support package.json field)\r\n\r\nCo-authored-by: Michal Piechowiak <misiek.piechowiak@gmail.com>\r\nCo-authored-by: gatsbybot <mathews.kyle+gatsbybot@gmail.com>",

+      "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,209 @@\n+# Gatsby Recipes\n+\n+Gatsby Recipes is framework for automating common Gatsby tasks. Recipes are MDX\n+files which, when run by our interpretor, perform common actions like installing\n+NPM packages, installing plugins, creating pages, etc.\n+\n+It's designed to be extensible so new capabilities can be added which allow\n+Recipes to automate more things.\n+\n+We chose MDX to allow for a literate programming style of writing recipes which\n+enables us to port our dozens of recipes from\n+https://www.gatsbyjs.org/docs/recipes/ as well as in the future, entire\n+tutorials.\n+\n+[Read more about Recipes on the RFC](https://github.com/gatsbyjs/gatsby/pull/22610)\n+\n+There's an umbrella issue for testing / using Recipes during its incubation stage.\n+\n+Follow the issue for updates!\n+\n+https://github.com/gatsbyjs/gatsby/issues/22991\n+\n+## Recipe setup\n+\n+Upgrade the global gatsby-cli package to the latest with recipes.\n+\n+```shell\n+npm install -g gatsby-cli@latest\n+```\n+\n+To confirm that this worked, run `gatsby --help` in your terminal. The output should show the recipes command.\n+\n+### Running an example recipe\n+\n+Now you can test out recipes! Start with a recipe for installing `emotion` by following these steps:\n+\n+1. Create a new Hello World Gatsby site:\n+\n+```shell\n+gatsby new try-emotion https://github.com/gatsbyjs/gatsby-starter-hello-world\n+```\n+\n+1. Navigate into that project directory:\n+\n+```shell\n+cd try-emotion\n+```\n+\n+1. Now you can run the `emotion` recipe with this command:\n+\n+```shell\n+gatsby recipes emotion\n+```\n+\n+![Terminal showing \"gatsby recipes emotion\" output](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1424573/79452177-f3362f00-7fa4-11ea-903a-e28472bf95b6.png)\n+\n+You can see a list of other recipes to run by running `gatsby recipes`\n+\n+![Terminal showing recipes list](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1424573/79452254-14971b00-7fa5-11ea-9bdf-021c341afb10.png)\n+\n+## Developing Recipes\n+\n+### An example MDX recipe\n+\n+Here's how you would write the `gatsby recipes emotion` recipe you just ran:\n+\n+```mdx\n+# Setup Gatsby with Emotion\n+\n+[Emotion](https://emotion.sh/) is a powerful CSS-in-JS library that supports both inline CSS styles and styled components. You can use each styling feature individually or together in the same file.\n+\n+<!-- use three dashes to separate steps of the recipe -->\n+\n+---\n+\n+Install necessary NPM packages\n+\n+<!-- refer to the API in this doc to see what APIs are available, like `NPMPackage` -->\n+\n+<NPMPackage name=\"gatsby-plugin-emotion\" />\n+<NPMPackage name=\"@emotion/core\" />\n+<NPMPackage name=\"@emotion/styled\" />\n+\n+---\n+\n+Install the Emotion plugin in gatsby-config.js\n+\n+<GatsbyPlugin name=\"gatsby-plugin-emotion\" />\n+\n+---\n+\n+Sweet, now it's ready to go.\n+\n+Let's also write out an example page you can use to play\n+with Emotion.\n+\n+<File\n+  path=\"src/pages/emotion-example.js\"\n+  content=\"https://gist.githubusercontent.com/KyleAMathews/323bacd551df46e8e7b6146cbf827d0b/raw/5c60f168f30c505cff1ff2433e69dabe27ae9738/sample-emotion.js\"\n+/>\n+\n+---\n+\n+Read more about Emotion on the official Emotion docs site:\n+\n+https://emotion.sh/docs/introduction\n+```\n+\n+### How to run recipes\n+\n+You can run built-in recipes, ones you write locally, and ones people have posted online.\n+\n+To run a local recipe, make sure to start the path to the recipe with a period like `gatsby recipes ./my-cool-recipe.mdx`\n+\n+To run a remote recipe, just paste in the path to the recipe e.g. `gatsby recipes https://example.com/sweet-recipe.mdx`\n+\n+### Recipe API\n+\n+#### `<GatsbyPlugin>`\n+\n+Installs a Gatsby Plugin in the site's `gatsby-config.js`.\n+\n+Soon will support options.\n+\n+```jsx\n+<GatsbyPlugin name=\"gatsby-plugin-emotion\" />\n+```\n+\n+##### props\n+\n+- **name** name of the plugin\n+\n+#### `<GatsbyShadowFile>`\n+\n+<GatsbyShadowFile theme=\"gatsby-theme-blog\" path=\"src/components/seo.js\" />\n+\n+##### props\n+\n+- **theme** the name of the theme (or plugin) which provides the file you'd like to shadow\n+- **path** the path to the file within the theme. E.g. the example file above lives at `node_modules/gatsby-theme-blog/src/components/seo.js`\n+\n+#### `<NPMPackage>`\n+\n+`<NPMPackage name=\"lodash\" version=\"latest\" />`\n+\n+##### props\n+\n+- **name**: name of the package(s) to install. Takes a string or an array of strings.\n+- **version**: defaults to latest\n+- **dependencyType**: defaults to `production`. Other options include `development`\n+\n+#### `<NPMScript>`\n+\n+`<NPMScript name=\"test\" command=\"jest\" />`\n+\n+##### props\n+\n+- **name:** name of the command\n+- **command** the command that's run when the script is called\n+\n+#### `<File>`\n+\n+<File path=\"test.md\" content=\"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KyleAMathews/test-recipes/master/gatsby-recipe-jest.mdx\" />\n+\n+##### props\n+\n+- **path** path to the file that should be created. The path is local to the root of the Node.js project (where the package.json is)\n+- **content** URL to the content that should be written to the path. Eventually we'll support directly putting content here after some fixees to MDX.\n+\n+> Note that this content is stored in a [GitHub gist](https://gist.github.com/). When linking to a gist you'll want to click on the \"Raw\" button and copy the URL from that page.\n+\n+## FAQ / common issues\n+\n+### Q) My recipe is combining steps instead of running them seperately!\n+\n+We use the `---` break syntax from Markdown to separate steps.\n+\n+One quirk with it is for it to work, it must have an empty line above it.\n+\n+So this will work:\n+\n+```mdx\n+# Recipes\n+\n+---\n+\n+a step\n+\n+<File src=\"something.txt\" content=\"something\" />\n+```\n+\n+But this won't\n+\n+```mdx\n+# Recipes\n+\n+---\n+\n+a step\n+\n+<File src=\"something.txt\" content=\"something\" />\n+```\n+\n+### Q) What kind of recipe should I write?\n+\n+If you’d like to write a recipe, there are two great places to get an idea:\n+\n+- Think of a task that took you more time than other tasks in the last Gatsby site you built. Is there a way to automate any part of that task?\n+- Look at this list of recipes in the Gatsby docs. Many of these can be partially or fully automated through creating a recipe `mdx` file. https://www.gatsbyjs.org/docs/recipes/"

+      "blob_url": "https://github.com/gatsbyjs/gatsby/blob/c59a42185674d25a5afcb32c5b05788e8b655b1e/packages%2Fgatsby-recipes%2Frecipes%2Fcypress.mdx",
+      "raw_url": "https://github.com/gatsbyjs/gatsby/raw/c59a42185674d25a5afcb32c5b05788e8b655b1e/packages%2Fgatsby-recipes%2Frecipes%2Fcypress.mdx",
+      "contents_url": "https://api.github.com/repos/gatsbyjs/gatsby/contents/packages%2Fgatsby-recipes%2Frecipes%2Fcypress.mdx?ref=c59a42185674d25a5afcb32c5b05788e8b655b1e",
+      "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@\n+Gatsby and Cypress can be used together seamlessly (and should be!). [Cypress](https://cypress.io) enables you to run end-to-end tests on your client-side application, which is what Gatsby produces.\n+\n+First, we'll want to install Cypress and additional dependencies.\n+\n+---\n+\n+<NPMPackage name=\"cypress\" dependencyType=\"development\" />\n+<NPMPackage name=\"gatsby-cypress\" dependencyType=\"development\" />\n+<NPMPackage name=\"start-server-and-test\" dependencyType=\"development\" />\n+\n+---\n+\n+Well look at that — we've added dependencies to your package.json and we also installed a useful package `gatsby-cypress`. `gatsby-cypress` exposes additional Cypress functionality which makes Gatsby and Cypress work together just a bit more nicely. We'll show that later with our first test, but hold tight for just a bit because first we need to scaffold out some boilerplate files for Cypress.\n+\n+---\n+\n+<File\n+ path=\"cypress/plugins/index.js\"\n+ content={`https://gist.github.com/KyleAMathews/a88885cf6a52b8a0c654319ab544d958/raw/b434660dd8b695eca3b38bf1b40303c705c1aec5/plugins-index.js`}\n+/>\n+\n+<File\n+ path=\"cypress/support/index.js\"\n+ content={`https://gist.github.com/KyleAMathews/a88885cf6a52b8a0c654319ab544d958/raw/b434660dd8b695eca3b38bf1b40303c705c1aec5/support-index.js`}\n+/>\n+\n+---\n+\n+Cool cool! So we created a local `cypress` folder with two sub-folders, `support` and `plugins`. We've also automatically included all the nice `gatsby-cypress` utilities, which we can now use in our first test.\n+\n+---\n+\n+<File\n+ path=\"cypress/integration/home-page/home-page.js\"\n+ content={`https://gist.github.com/KyleAMathews/a88885cf6a52b8a0c654319ab544d958/raw/b434660dd8b695eca3b38bf1b40303c705c1aec5/home-page-home-page.js`}\n+/>\n+\n+---\n+\n+Our first test! You'll notice it's failing. This is intentional -- we'd like you to run the test and fix it. This raises a question -- how do you run a Cypress test? Easy peasy.\n+\n+---\n+\n+<NPMScript\n+  name=\"develop\"\n+  command=\"gatsby develop\"\n+/>\n+\n+<NPMScript\n+  name=\"cy:open\"\n+  command=\"cypress open\"\n+/>\n+\n+<NPMScript\n+  name=\"test:e2e\"\n+  command=\"start-server-and-test develop http://localhost:8000 cy:open\"\n+/>\n+\n+---\n+\n+Nifty! We've added two scripts:\n+\n+- `start-server-and-test`: This spins up a local Gatsby development server and \"waits\" until it's live so we can then run our tests\n+- `test:e2e`: This is the command you'll use to run your tests.\n+\n+Let's give it a try. Run the following command in your terminal.\n+\n+npm run test:e2e\n+\n+Now you'll have a way to run and validate your Cypress tests with the dream-team combo of Gatsby and Cypress."

+      "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,40 @@\n+# Add a custom ESLint config\n+\n+## Introduction to ESLint\n+ESLint is an open source JavaScript linting utility. Code linting is a type of\n+static analysis that is frequently used to find problematic patterns. There are\n+code linters for most programming languages, and compilers sometimes\n+incorporate linting into the compilation process.\n+\n+JavaScript, being a dynamic and loosely-typed language, is especially prone to\n+developer error. Without the benefit of a compilation process, JavaScript code\n+is typically executed in order to find syntax or other errors. Linting tools\n+like ESLint allow developers to discover problems with their JavaScript code\n+without executing it.\n+\n+## Why use this recipe\n+\n+Gatsby ships with a built-in ESLint setup. For most users,\n+our built-in ESlint setup is all you need. If you know however that you’d like\n+to customize your ESlint config e.g. your company has their own custom ESlint\n+setup, this recipe sets this up for you.\n+\n+You’ll replicate (mostly) the ESLint config Gatsby ships with so you can then\n+add additional presets, plugins, and rules.\n+\n+---\n+\n+Install necessary packages\n+\n+<NPMPackage name=\"eslint-config-react-app\" dependencyType={\"development\"} />\n+\n+---\n+\n+<File\n+  path=\".eslintrc.js\"\n+  content='https://gist.github.com/KyleAMathews/5c4cfa4f58cc2707094f3ae5048e72f6'/>\n+\n+---\n+\n+ESlint is now installed! You can edit the eslint config by opening\n+`.eslintrc.js` in your code editor."

+      "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@\n+# Setup gatsby-plugin-layout\n+Setup [gatsby-plugin-layout](https://www.gatsbyjs.org/packages/gatsby-plugin-layout/?=gatsby%20layout)\n+\n+This plugin enables adding components which live above the page components and persist across page changes.\n+\n+This can be helpful for:\n+\n+- Persisting layout between page changes for e.g. animating navigation\n+- Storing state when navigating pages\n+- Custom error handling using componentDidCatch\n+- Inject additional data into pages using React Context.\n+\n+---\n+\n+Install necessary NPM packages\n+\n+<NPMPackage name=\"gatsby-plugin-layout\"/>\n+\n+---\n+\n+Install the Layout plugin in gatsby-config.js\n+\n+<GatsbyPlugin name=\"gatsby-plugin-layout\"/>\n+\n+---\n+\n+Sweet, now it's ready to go!\n+\n+Let's also write out a sample layout component to get started with.\n+\n+<File\n+    path=\"src/layouts/index.js\"\n+    content=\"https://gist.github.com/JeremyTheModernist/be673e8641c61e6a427124acad1e05da\"\n+/>\n+\n+---\n+\n+Read more about the documentation for Gatsby Layout Component here:\n+https://www.gatsbyjs.org/packages/gatsby-plugin-lay"

+      "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,29 @@\n+# Setup Gatsby Theme Blog\n+\n+[Gatsby theme blog](https://www.gatsbyjs.org/packages/gatsby-theme-blog/) is a great theme for adding blog functionality to your site.\n+\n+---\n+\n+Install necessary NPM packages\n+\n+<NPMPackage name=\"gatsby-theme-blog\" />\n+<NPMPackage name=\"gatsby-theme-blog-core\" />\n+\n+---\n+\n+Install the gatsby-theme-blog plugin in gatsby-config.js\n+\n+<GatsbyPlugin name=\"gatsby-theme-blog\" />\n+\n+---\n+Now let's add a post!\n+\n+<File path=\"content/posts/first-blog.md\" content=\"https://gist.githubusercontent.com/laurieontech/7a0c01a1cee0d99b74a519faa7a83d4a/raw/589dcc93ee2fca4bdedfab04fc16736dd5d9201e/first-blog.md\" />\n+\n+---\n+\n+Sweet, now it's ready to go.\n+\n+Note that for the moment you'll need to delete your src/pages/index.js file.\n+\n+---"

+      "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,46 @@\n+# Add Jest\n+\n+This recipe helps you setup Jest in your Gatsby site to test components and utilities\n+\n+<Config\n+  name=\"gatsbyjs/add-jest\"\n+/>\n+\n+---\n+\n+Installing the `jest` package\n+\n+<NPMPackage name=\"jest\" />\n+\n+---\n+\n+Adding some jest test files for you to play with\n+\n+<File\n+  path=\"src/jest-example/sum.js\"\n+  content=\"https://gist.github.com/KyleAMathews/3267b3e09b23dd693aa996b23dfd2d6f/raw/f7c8fa25c295421d8826037b40ac924a33aebf15/sum.js\"\n+/>\n+\n+<File\n+  path=\"src/jest-example/sum.test.js\"\n+  content=\"https://gist.github.com/KyleAMathews/3267b3e09b23dd693aa996b23dfd2d6f/raw/f7c8fa25c295421d8826037b40ac924a33aebf15/sum.test.js\"\n+/>\n+\n+---\n+\n+Adding a `test` & `test:watch` scripts to your package.json.\n+\n+Now Try running `npm run test` — jest will run your test!\n+\n+While writing tests you can run `npm run test:watch` and tests will re-run\n+as you edit them.\n+\n+<NPMScript\n+  name=\"test\"\n+  command=\"jest\"\n+/>\n+\n+<NPMScript\n+  name=\"test:watch\"\n+  command=\"jest --watch\"\n+/>"

+      "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,59 @@\n+# Automaically run Prettier on commits\n+\n+Make sure all of your code is run through Prettier when you commit it to git.\n+We achieve this by configuring prettier to run on git hooks using husky and\n+lint-staged.\n+\n+---\n+\n+Install packages.\n+\n+<NPMPackage name=\"husky\" />\n+<NPMPackage name=\"prettier\" />\n+<NPMPackage name=\"lint-staged\" />\n+\n+---\n+\n+Implement git hooks for prettier.\n+\n+<NPMPackageJson\n+  name=\"husky\"\n+  value={{\n+    \"hooks\": {\n+      \"pre-commit\": \"lint-staged\"\n+    }\n+  }}\n+/>\n+<NPMPackageJson\n+  name=\"lint-staged\"\n+  value={{\n+    \"*.{js,md,mdx,json}\": [\n+      \"prettier --write\"\n+    ]\n+  }}\n+/>\n+\n+---\n+\n+Write prettier config files.\n+\n+<File\n+  path=\".prettierrc\"\n+  content={`{\n+  \"semi\": false,\n+  \"singleQuote\": true,\n+  \"trailingComma\": \"none\"\n+}`}\n+/>\n+<File\n+  path=\".prettierignore\"\n+  content={`.cache\n+public\n+node_modules\n+`}\n+/>\n+\n+---\n+\n+Prettier, husky, and lint-staged are now installed! You can edit your `.prettierrc`\n+if you'd like to change your prettier configuration."

+      "patch": "@@ -0,0 +1,31 @@\n+const babel = require(`@babel/standalone`)\n+const jsxSyntax = require(`@babel/plugin-syntax-jsx`)\n+\n+const BabelPluginRemoveElementByName = (api, { names }) => {\n+  return {\n+    visitor: {\n+      JSXElement(path) {\n+        if (names.includes(path.node.openingElement.name.name)) {\n+          path.remove()\n+        }\n+      },\n+    },\n+  }\n+}\n+\n+module.exports = (src, options) => {\n+  try {\n+    const { code } = babel.transform(`<>${src}</>`, {\n+      configFile: false,\n+      plugins: [[BabelPluginRemoveElementByName, options], jsxSyntax],\n+    })\n+\n+    return code.replace(/^<>/, ``).replace(/<\\/>;$/, ``)\n+  } catch (e) {\n+    console.log(e)\n+  }\n+\n+  return null\n+}\n+\n+module.exports.BabelPluginRemoveElementByName = BabelPluginRemoveElementByName"

+const fs = require(`fs-extra`)
+const path = require(`path`)
+const babel = require(`@babel/core`)
+const Joi = require(`@hapi/joi`)
+const glob = require(`glob`)
+const prettier = require(`prettier`)
+
+const declare = require(`@babel/helper-plugin-utils`).declare
+
+const getDiff = require(`../utils/get-diff`)
+const resourceSchema = require(`../resource-schema`)
+const fileExists = filePath => fs.existsSync(filePath)
+
+const listShadowableFilesForTheme = (directory, theme) => {
+  const fullThemePath = path.join(directory, `node_modules`, theme, `src`)
+  const shadowableThemeFiles = glob.sync(fullThemePath + `/**/*.*`, {
+    follow: true,
+  })
+
+  const toShadowPath = filePath => {
+    const themePath = filePath.replace(fullThemePath, ``)
+    return path.join(`src`, theme, themePath)
+  }
+
+  const shadowPaths = shadowableThemeFiles.map(toShadowPath)
+
+  const shadowedFiles = shadowPaths.filter(fileExists)
+  const shadowableFiles = shadowPaths.filter(filePath => !fileExists(filePath))
+
+  return { shadowedFiles, shadowableFiles }
+}
+
+const isDefaultExport = node => {
+  if (!node || node.type !== `MemberExpression`) {
+    return false
+  }
+
+  const { object, property } = node
+
+  if (object.type !== `Identifier` || object.name !== `module`) return false
+  if (property.type !== `Identifier` || property.name !== `exports`)
+    return false
+
+  return true
+}
+
+const getValueFromLiteral = node => {
+  if (node.type === `StringLiteral`) {
+    return node.value
+  }
+
+  if (node.type === `TemplateLiteral`) {
+    return node.quasis[0].value.raw
+  }
+
+  return null
+}
+
+const getNameForPlugin = node => {
+  if (node.type === `StringLiteral` || node.type === `TemplateLiteral`) {
+    return getValueFromLiteral(node)
+  }
+
+  if (node.type === `ObjectExpression`) {
+    const resolve = node.properties.find(p => p.key.name === `resolve`)
+    return resolve ? getValueFromLiteral(resolve.value) : null
+  }
+
+  return null
+}
+
+const addPluginToConfig = (src, pluginName) => {
+  const addPlugins = new BabelPluginAddPluginsToGatsbyConfig({
+    pluginOrThemeName: pluginName,
+    shouldAdd: true,
+  })
+
+  const { code } = babel.transform(src, {
+    plugins: [addPlugins.plugin],
+    configFile: false,
+  })
+
+  return code
+}
+
+const getPluginsFromConfig = src => {
+  const getPlugins = new BabelPluginGetPluginsFromGatsbyConfig()
+
+  babel.transform(src, {
+    plugins: [getPlugins.plugin],
+    configFile: false,
+  })
+
+  return getPlugins.state
+}
+
+const create = async ({ root }, { name }) => {
+  const configPath = path.join(root, `gatsby-config.js`)
+  const configSrc = await fs.readFile(configPath, `utf8`)
+
+  const prettierConfig = await prettier.resolveConfig(root)
+
+  let code = addPluginToConfig(configSrc, name)
+  code = prettier.format(code, { ...prettierConfig, parser: `babel` })
+
+  await fs.writeFile(configPath, code)
+
+  return await read({ root }, name)
+}
+
+const read = async ({ root }, id) => {
+  const configPath = path.join(root, `gatsby-config.js`)
+  const configSrc = await fs.readFile(configPath, `utf8`)
+
+  const name = getPluginsFromConfig(configSrc).find(name => name === id)
+
+  if (name) {
+    return { id, name, _message: `Installed ${id} in gatsby-config.js` }
+  } else {
+    return undefined
+  }
+}
+
+const destroy = async ({ root }, { name }) => {
+  const configPath = path.join(root, `gatsby-config.js`)
+  const configSrc = await fs.readFile(configPath, `utf8`)
+
+  const addPlugins = new BabelPluginAddPluginsToGatsbyConfig({
+    pluginOrThemeName: name,
+    shouldAdd: false,
+  })
+
+  const { code } = babel.transform(configSrc, {
+    plugins: [addPlugins.plugin],
+    configFile: false,
+  })
+
+  await fs.writeFile(configPath, code)
+}
+
+class BabelPluginAddPluginsToGatsbyConfig {
+  constructor({ pluginOrThemeName, shouldAdd }) {
+    this.plugin = declare(api => {
+      api.assertVersion(7)
+
+      const { types: t } = api
+      return {
+        visitor: {
+          ExpressionStatement(path) {
+            const { node } = path
+            const { left, right } = node.expression
+
+            if (!isDefaultExport(left)) {
+              return
+            }
+
+            const plugins = right.properties.find(p => p.key.name === `plugins`)
+
+            if (shouldAdd) {
+              const pluginNames = plugins.value.elements.map(getNameForPlugin)
+              const exists = pluginNames.includes(pluginOrThemeName)
+              if (!exists) {
+                plugins.value.elements.push(t.stringLiteral(pluginOrThemeName))
+              }
+            } else {
+              plugins.value.elements = plugins.value.elements.filter(
+                node => getNameForPlugin(node) !== pluginOrThemeName
+              )
+            }
+
+            path.stop()
+          },
+        },
+      }
+    })
+  }
+}
+
+class BabelPluginGetPluginsFromGatsbyConfig {
+  constructor() {
+    this.state = []
+
+    this.plugin = declare(api => {
+      api.assertVersion(7)
+
+      return {
+        visitor: {
+          ExpressionStatement: path => {
+            const { node } = path
+            const { left, right } = node.expression
+
+            if (!isDefaultExport(left)) {
+              return
+            }
+
+            const plugins = right.properties.find(p => p.key.name === `plugins`)
+
+            plugins.value.elements.map(node => {
+              this.state.push(getNameForPlugin(node))
+            })
+          },
+        },
+      }
+    })
+  }
+}
+
+module.exports.addPluginToConfig = addPluginToConfig
+module.exports.getPluginsFromConfig = getPluginsFromConfig
+
+module.exports.create = create
+module.exports.update = create
+module.exports.read = read
+module.exports.destroy = destroy
+module.exports.config = {}
+
+module.exports.all = async ({ root }) => {
+  const configPath = path.join(root, `gatsby-config.js`)
+  const src = await fs.readFile(configPath, `utf8`)
+  const plugins = getPluginsFromConfig(src)
+
+  // TODO: Consider mapping to read function
+  return plugins.map(name => {
+    const { shadowedFiles, shadowableFiles } = listShadowableFilesForTheme(
+      root,
+      name
+    )
+
+    return {
+      id: name,
+      name,
+      shadowedFiles,
+      shadowableFiles,
+    }
+  })
+}
+
+const schema = {
+  name: Joi.string(),
+  shadowableFiles: Joi.array().items(Joi.string()),
+  shadowedFiles: Joi.array().items(Joi.string()),
+  ...resourceSchema,
+}
+
+const validate = resource =>
+  Joi.validate(resource, schema, { abortEarly: false })
+
+exports.schema = schema
+exports.validate = validate
+
+module.exports.plan = async ({ root }, { id, name }) => {
+  const fullName = id || name
+  const configPath = path.join(root, `gatsby-config.js`)
+  const prettierConfig = await prettier.resolveConfig(root)
+  let src = await fs.readFile(configPath, `utf8`)
+  src = prettier.format(src, {
+    ...prettierConfig,
+    parser: `babel`,
+  })
+  let newContents = addPluginToConfig(src, fullName)
+  newContents = prettier.format(newContents, {
+    ...prettierConfig,
+    parser: `babel`,
+  })
+  const diff = await getDiff(src, newContents)
+
+  return {
+    id: fullName,
+    name,
+    diff,
+    currentState: src,
+    newState: newContents,
+    describe: `Install ${fullName} in gatsby-config.js`,
+  }
+}

diff --git a/tmp/verify_shadow.js b/tmp/verify_shadow.js
new file mode 100644
index 000000000..69efbd8bb
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tmp/verify_shadow.js
@@ -0,0 +1,39 @@
+const path = require(`path`)
+const fs = require(`fs-extra`)
+const rimraf = require(`rimraf`)
+
+const base = `/workspace/repo/packages/gatsby/src/recipes/providers`
+const shadowFile = require(path.join(base, `gatsby/shadow-file.js`))
+const resourceSchema = require(path.join(base, `resource-schema.js`))
+const Joi = require(`@hapi/joi`)
+
+const root = path.join(base, `gatsby/fixtures`)
+const cleanup = () => rimraf.sync(path.join(root, `src`))
+
+;(async () => {
+  cleanup()
+  const context = { root }
+  const initialObject = { theme: `gatsby-theme-blog`, path: `src/components/author.js` }
+
+  const createPlan = await shadowFile.plan(context, initialObject)
+  console.log(`--- create plan ---`); console.log(JSON.stringify(createPlan, null, 2))
+
+  const createResponse = await shadowFile.create(context, initialObject)
+  const v = Joi.validate(createResponse, { ...shadowFile.schema, ...resourceSchema })
+  console.log(`--- create (validate error: ${v.error}) ---`); console.log(JSON.stringify(createResponse, null, 2))
+
+  const readResponse = await shadowFile.read(context, createResponse.id)
+  console.log(`read == create:`, JSON.stringify(readResponse) === JSON.stringify(createResponse))
+
+  const updatedResource = { ...readResponse, ...initialObject }
+  const updatePlan = await shadowFile.plan(context, updatedResource)
+  console.log(`--- update plan describe:`, updatePlan.describe, `diff:`, JSON.stringify(updatePlan.diff))
+
+  const updateResponse = await shadowFile.update(context, updatedResource)
+  const destroyResponse = await shadowFile.destroy(context, updateResponse)
+  console.log(`--- destroy ---`); console.log(JSON.stringify(destroyResponse, null, 2))
+
+  const postDestroy = await shadowFile.read(context, createResponse.id)
+  console.log(`post-destroy read undefined:`, postDestroy === undefined)
+  cleanup()
+})().catch(e => { console.error(`ERROR`, e); process.exit(1) })

If the certificate is signed by a private ca, then include that ca's certificate using this flag in order for node to trust the cert/key pair\r\n3. +      "message": "perf(gatsby): Support `lte` for indexed fast filters (#22932)\n\n* Rename function to better fit what it returns\r\n\r\n* Use `filterCacheKey` more consistently\r\n\r\n* Consistency around `nodesPerValue`\r\n\r\n* Fix the name and typing of array of sets of nodes\r\n\r\n* Fix typing, fix perf bug\r\n\r\nThe typing of the array of caches was incorrect (see previous commit too).\r\n\r\nThe sort, affected in this commit, was sorting by `.length`, but the value is a `Set` so the intention was to sort by `.size` since its `.length` will always be `undefined`. This won't change semantics, just meant that the sort didn't do anything, leading to a sub-optimal performance.\r\n\r\n* Extend the `FilterCache` type to support op-specific meta data\r\n\r\n* Replace wild usage of `FilterType`\r\n\r\n* Refactor some old comments / naming to be consistent with current code / types\r\n\r\n* Suggested changes\r\n\r\nFollowup commits suggested by @vladar in https://github.com/gatsbyjs/gatsby/pull/22742\r\n\r\n* Enable `lte` for fast filters\r\n\r\n* Mandatory lint/type fix commit\r\n\r\n* And the loki commit\r\n\r\n* Enable/disable query and eleeMatch ops in one place\r\n\r\n* Fix tests, fix lte binary search lookup\r\n\r\n* Support `null` properly and handle not found binary search case\r\n\r\nThe binary search should not return an arbitrary node, but rather a signal value (`undefined` in this case) that it failed somehow. It shouldn't, but who knows.\r\n\r\nThe `null` case was a bit more work because it affects typign and all kinds of weird comparing edge cases. There's also a distinction between how `eq` treats `null` target values versus how `lte` treats them. So I had to encode them differently in the cache. Hence the type update.\r\n\r\n* Sigh, this is why I had to introduce that type in the first place\r\n\r\n* Forgot to remove an argument from followup work\r\n\r\n* Apply suggestions",
